_note: English versions of the park's 10 suggested routes. Names and descriptions translated from the Macedonian text in park-map-2020.json; ends are [lat, lon] of each trailhead, taken from the park's start markers.

1.name: Velgoshti - Letnica - Ramne - Ohrid visitor centre
1.text: A west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. The lower part runs through low vegetation, the upper part through forest. The ground is hard and stony, with lush grass in places. In several places, especially below Letnica and at the spot called Skala, the trail crosses streams that are easy to cross for most of the year.

2.name: Ramne - Letnica - Visok Vrv - Krstec - Velestovo
2.text: A mostly west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. Parts run through low vegetation, higher parts through forest, and the highest stretch is open ground with wide views. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places. In several places, especially below Letnica and at Skala, the trail crosses streams that are easy to cross for most of the year.

3.name: Velestovo - Krstec - Tri Mazhi peak - Studino - Elshani
3.text: A long combined tour through nearly every kind of habitat in the park. The start and the end face west; higher up the route follows ridges, dense belts of forest and wide open karst fields. Most of the height is gained at the start, and after that the ups and downs are gentle enough for relaxed walking. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places. On the ridge path from Krstec to Cresha it's firm earth and stones, and the middle section is mostly rocky. Excellent views over all of Galičica and the wider region.

4.name: Elshani - Bugarska Chuka - Lako Signoj - Galičica pass
4.text: Mostly a ridge walk, and mostly on soft ground that's pleasant underfoot, except from Elshani up to Bugarska Chuka, where it's hard and stony. Apart from short stretches above Elshani there's no vegetation along the path. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow. It passes many historic sites, mostly from the First World War. The park calls it one of the most attractive trails in Macedonia, for the sense of space and the views.

5.name: Galičica pass - Magaro peak - Galičica pass
5.text: Mostly a ridge walk on hard, stony ground. Through the beech forest the path is well cleared; above it there's no vegetation along the path. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow. Above the forest it becomes a loop that takes in nearly every landform in this part of the mountain. The park recommends going up from the west along the eastern ridge, past the big metal radio reflector, and coming down the south side through the stony dry valley. The trail passes many First World War sites. It runs through the strict protection zone, so leaving the trail isn't allowed.

6.name: Dva Javora - Sharbojca house - Samotska Dupka cave - Velestovo
6.text: Crosses the middle of the mountain on very gentle terrain, the ups and downs nearly following the contour lines. The ground is mostly hard and stony, with soft grass in parts of the karst fields. There's no vegetation along the path except short stretches near Samotska Dupka cave. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow.

7.name: Velestovo - Elen Vrv - Konjsko - Elshani
7.text: A west-facing trail with the climbing spread fairly evenly. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places.

8.name: Peshtani - St Spas - Galičica pass - Peshtani
8.text: A west-facing trail with fairly even, steady climbing that the park calls distinctly sporty. The lower part runs through low vegetation, the upper part through forest. The ground is hard and stony, grassy in places.

9.name: Oteshevo - Goga peak - Sharbojca mountain house
9.text: Crosses the eastern and central parts of the mountain with steady climbs and a strongly sporty character. The ground is mostly hard and stony, with soft grass in parts of the karst fields. In its lower half the path runs through dense tall forest, easy to pass, though in places big fallen trunks lie across it. For most of the way the trail is clear and, in good visibility, easy to follow.

10.name: Stenje - Konjsko along Lake Prespa
10.text: Follows the shore of Lake Prespa on stony, hard but mostly pleasant ground. Since it keeps to the shoreline, the ups and downs are insignificant. The low vegetation on either side tends to overgrow the path, so in places you may have to push through, mostly through grass.

start_fix._note: Park start markers that don't match the start they're labelled with. Index = variant (0 or 1).
